summary: Scoped E2E test of BETA registration-request -> admin approval -> login-by-ID workflow + product permanent delete + admin security. Backend: 20/21 pytest cases pass (new file /app/backend/tests/test_regrequest_flow.py). Frontend: registration pending screen, duplicate guard, admin Registration Requests card, approve (ANJ000177 generated, RED/active), reject, and product permanent delete all work. TWO blocking bugs found: (1) approving an EMAIL-LESS request returns 500 (DuplicateKeyError on non-sparse unique users.email index - only ONE null-email user can ever exist); (2) /login identifier input is type='email' + required, so HTML5 validation blocks submit for Distributor ID and mobile - login-by-ID is impossible in the UI even though the backend supports it.

critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error when the request has no email. server.py:110 creates `db.users.create_index('email', unique=True)` WITHOUT sparse/partial filter, and approve inserts email:None -> pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError: E11000 dup key users.email_1 { email: null }. Only the first email-less distributor (ANJ000172) could be created; every later email-optional approval fails. Reproduced via API and via Admin UI (toast 'Request failed with status code 500', row stays pending). Fix: create index with partialFilterExpression {email: {$type: 'string'}} (note: sparse alone does NOT help because null IS indexed), or omit the email key entirely when there is no email, and drop/rebuild the existing email_1 index.

minor.issue: No guard for already-approved/already-rejected requests (idempotently re-sets status, returns 200). Approve correctly 400s on double-approve.
Returns all requests (pending/approved/rejected) with no status filter or pagination beyond 500; frontend filters client-side. Fine now, will not scale.

ui_bugs.issue: Identifier field is <Input type="email" required> and labelled 'Email'. Entering a Distributor ID (ANJ000177) or a 10-digit mobile makes checkValidity()=false, so the browser blocks form submit and NO API call is made -> approved email-less/ID-based distributors cannot log in from the UI. Backend /api/auth/login accepts DID/mobile/email (verified 200 via API). Fix: type='text' and label 'Distributor ID / Mobile / Email'.
Add-product button label uses t('cta.getStarted') so it renders 'Get Started' instead of 'Add Product'.

integration_issues.flow: Admin approve of email-less registration request
integration_issues.issue: Backend 500 surfaces only as a generic 'Request failed with status code 500' toast; row remains pending with no actionable message.

issues: Layout, contrast and spacing look correct; pending badge readable. No issues found.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix users.email unique index (partialFilterExpression email:{$type:'string'}) AND drop the existing email_1 index so email-optional approvals stop 500ing; then re-run the email-less approve test.
CRITICAL: Change /login identifier input to type='text' (remove email validation) and relabel to 'Distributor ID / Mobile / Email' so login-by-ID/mobile actually works in the UI.
Optional: guard reject() against already-approved requests; surface backend error detail in the approve toast.
Optional: fix Add Product button label (uses cta.getStarted).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:110 `db.users.create_index('email', unique=True)` is incompatible with the new email-optional registration; must be partial/unique-on-string.
admin_routes.py approve_registration_request has no try/except around users.insert_one, so DB constraint violations leak as 500 instead of a 400/409 with a clear message.

auth_routes.py login(): brute-force counter keys only on the lowercased raw identifier, so DID vs mobile vs email attempts are counted separately (lockout can be bypassed by rotating identifier form).

rca_of_the_issue: Bug 1: MongoDB unique index on users.email was created without a partial filter. Since MongoDB indexes null values, the second user document with email:null violates uniqueness -> DuplicateKeyError -> unhandled 500 in approve_registration_request. Bug 2: Login.js kept the legacy email-only input (type='email' required) after the backend was widened to accept Distributor ID / mobile, so the browser's own constraint validation prevents submission for non-email identifiers.
